newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids down, movement slow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids down, movement slow.

text.p: Dark northern spring wheat cash bids were lower on Monday and movement was slow as residual effects from last week's heavy snows shut down roads and rail lines, cash grain dealers said.
"There's a little bit of wheat being sold but (farmers) are not breaking down the door," one merchant said.

Weeks of heavy snow and cold temperatures hampered movement. Although temperatures were warmer Monday, snow and ice covered railroad tracks and many signals and switches were malfunctioning, a Montana dealer said..
"It's affecting the railroad," he said. "If you bought wheat from farmers right now it would be a question of when you could move it."

But activity was expected to pick up in Minnesota in the next couple of weeks, one merchant said. Farmers had been storing the grain to defer income and tax payments until next year, but many planned to sell in January.
